subject: Production: QuantumBridge - elevated 5xx/429, timeouts and retry amplification
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha@quantumbridge.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Production: high 5xx/429 + timeouts affecting inference (QuantumBridge)

Irene,

We started seeing a sharp spike in 5xx and 429 responses to our inference calls beginning ~07:40 PST. Error rate is around 12% across our critical endpoints (was ~0.2% baseline). Customers are experiencing timeouts and automated retries which appear to be amplifying the load. Latency tail has gone from ~150ms to >3s and several jobs are failing completely.

Samples: request-ids: rb:7a8d9c, rb:7a8d9f, rb:7a8e01 (see attached error-sample.log). This is happening against our dedicated pool in us-west (QuantumBridge -> dedicated: qbridge-usw1-pool).

Impact: production traffic degraded for our chat assistant and billing reconciliation pipeline. We are at risk of missing SLA windows for enterprise customers. Please advise immediate mitigations and ETA.

Thanks,
Aisha Patel
Head of SRE, QuantumBridge
ops@quantumbridge.ai

Attachments: error-sample.log

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha@quantumbridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T08:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production: high 5xx/429 + timeouts affecting inference (QuantumBridge)

Thanks for the report, Aisha — I see the spike in our dashboards as well. I'm triaging now and have looped Ben from platform ops.

Immediate asks so we can scope mitigations:
- Can you confirm whether traffic pattern changed (burst from a small set of customers vs broad increase)?
- Are you doing any client-side aggressive retries/backoff that started around 07:30-07:45?
- If you can share a small time-window of the full request header for one of the failing request-ids that helps correlate.

We will do the following now:
1) Verify GPU pool utilization and queue depth for qbridge-usw1-pool.
2) Consider a routing policy change to move traffic to a hosted fallback model to stop retry amplification.
3) If needed, provision additional capacity to the dedicated pool as a hotfix.

Ben — can you take the lead on the pool metrics and quick mitigations? I will keep Aisha posted every 15–30 minutes.

Irene
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Aisha Patel <aisha@quantumbridge.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T08:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production: high 5xx/429 + timeouts affecting inference (QuantumBridge)

Quick summary of what I see from the platform side after a rapid triage:
- qbridge-usw1-pool GPUs at 100% sustained utilization since ~07:35.
- Queue depth spiked to ~18k pending requests at peak, average service time increased due to longer sequences; autoscaler attempted to add nodes but hit provider-side throttling and cooldowns — effective scaling lag ~6-8 minutes.
- 5xx burst correlates with queueing/timeouts at the runtime layer (OOM/retry backpressure) and a splash of 429s from the local per-pool rate limiter.
- Client retries are indeed amplifying the load — I can see repeated request-ids from the same client IP ranges.

Immediate mitigations applied / proposed (rolled out now or within minutes):
A) Routed 40% of traffic for QuantumBridge production routes to a hosted fallback model (rw-medium-compat) to break the retry loop. This was applied at 08:42 PST — monitoring now. (See runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/internal/routing-fallback)
B) Temporarily raised the per-pool rate limiter threshold for qbridge-usw1-pool to avoid premature 429s while we bring capacity up (small risk of increased queueing; mitigates client-side retries).
C) Requested a hot-provision of +4 GPUs to the dedicated pool; cloud provider nodal allocation in progress (estimated +15–25 mins) — tracking INC-8743.

Notes / next steps:
- We'll keep fallback routing until queue depth subsides and 5xx < 1%.
- Recommend QuantumBridge consider smoothing client retry backoff to reduce amplification — I can share suggested client settings.
- After stabilization, we'll do a postmortem and recommend autoscaler cooldown/tuning to avoid similar lag.

Attaching current capacity snapshot for the pool: capacity-metrics.png

Ben
Platform Ops (dedicated capacity)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Production: QuantumBridge - elevated 5xx/429, timeouts and retry amplification

Aisha — final update and next steps from our side.

Timeline & outcome:
- 08:42 PST: Fallback routing (40% -> rw-medium-compat) enabled — immediate reduction in client retries observed.
- 09:10 PST: 5xx dropped from ~12% to ~0.6%; latency tail returned to ~180–220ms for most requests.
- 09:30 PST: Provider allocated +4 GPUs to qbridge-usw1-pool; we verified capacity and drained queue.
- 10:05 PST: Full traffic routed back to dedicated pool, monitoring for 48 hours.

Action items we will deliver:
- Postmortem doc with timelines, root cause (autoscaler cooldown + provision throttling + retry amplification), and remediation plan: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1q2w3e-postmortem-qbridge (will be published within 72 hours).
- Ben will lead autoscaler tuning (reduce cooldown to 60s, add proactive buffer) and we will push safer routing defaults for dedicated pools.
- Marissa / Sales will follow up on proposed credit; Customer Success will approve final messaging.

Thanks for the fast escalation — please reach out if you see any regressions.

Irene Choi
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
